topic: Autobiographies of Famous Personalities (Sports, Politics, Arts)
description: An autobiography is a self-written account of a person's life. This study guide covers the major autobiographies of prominent figures in sports, politics, and the arts, which are highly crucial for the Static GK section of competitive exams.

sections.title: Basic Concepts
sections.description: Fundamental terminology related to literary genres concerning life histories.

key_concepts.explanation: An account of a person's life written by that person themselves.
An account of a person's life written, composed, or produced by someone else.
A collection of memories that an individual writes about moments or events, both public or private, that took place in the subject's life.

sections.title: Important Facts
sections.description: Exam-oriented one-liner facts related to the autobiographies of various global personalities.

important_facts.fact: The autobiography of the Mughal Emperor Babur, known as 'Baburnama' or 'Tuzuk-e-Babri', was originally written in the Chagatai Turkic language.
Adolf Hitler's autobiography is titled 'Mein Kampf', which translates from German to 'My Struggle'.
The famous autobiography of legendary Indian track and field athlete P.T. Usha is titled 'Golden Girl'.
Sania Mirza's autobiography, 'Ace Against Odds', chronicles her tennis career and the challenges she overcame.
Charlie Chaplin's 'My Autobiography' is considered one of the most important historical documents detailing the silent film era.
